items.example_en: The weather's nice, shall we eat outside?
items.note: Russian states it plainly, with no impersonal verb.

items.example_en: It's been raining since first thing.
items.note: Literally the rain goes. Same verb as walking.

items.example_en: It's snowing in the mountains.
items.note: Same construction as with rain.

items.example_en: It's cold today, put on a coat.
items.note: Impersonal adverb. мне холодно means I am cold.

items.example_en: What's the weather like where you are?
items.note: Unlike French and Spanish, weather and time are different words.

items.example_en: According to the forecast it'll rain tomorrow.
items.note: будет is the future of быть, needed because the present has no copula.

items.example_en: In spring everything blooms.
items.note: Seasons take the instrumental as an adverb: летом, осенью, зимой.

items.example_en: In summer we go to the seaside.
items.note: Neuter noun.

items.example: Этой зимой мы едем в горы.
items.example_en: We're going to the mountains this winter.
items.note: Plural of гора, with the stress moving to the first syllable.

items.example_en: The sea is calm today.
items.note: Going to the sea takes на: на море.

items.example: По воскресеньям мы гуляем в лесу.
items.example_en: On Sundays we walk in the forest.
items.note: Special locative form: в лесу, not в лесе.

items.example_en: Climate change is altering the seasons.

items.example: Это фильм, который я смотрел три раза.
items.example_en: It's a film I've watched three times.
items.note: который declines like an adjective and agrees with what it refers to.

items.example: Я всегда смотрю фильмы в оригинале.
items.example_en: I always watch films in the original language.
items.note: Russia dubs heavily, so this is worth asking for.

items.example_en: Turn on the Russian subtitles.
items.note: Watching with target-language subtitles is excellent practice.

items.example_en: I started a crime novel.
items.note: Also a romance, and the given name Roman. Context decides.

items.example_en: The series is long, but it's worth watching.
items.note: Impersonal стоит plus infinitive. Same verb as to cost.

items.example: Эту книгу я тебе очень советую.
items.example_en: I really recommend this book to you.
items.note: советовать takes the dative for the person advised.

items.example_en: I feel like going out somewhere tonight.
items.note: Softer than я хочу: the desire simply arises.

items.example_en: I'm meeting friends on Friday.
items.note: с plus instrumental. друзьями is an irregular plural.

items.example_en: Photography is my favourite hobby.
items.note: Indeclinable neuter noun.

items.example: Мы отмечали до трёх часов ночи.
items.example_en: We celebrated until three in the morning.
items.note: The everyday word for celebrating a birthday or a holiday.

items.example_en: How about a film tonight?
items.note: Takes the genitive: как насчёт кофе?

items.example_en: Where and when shall we meet?
items.note: The present tense covers the near-future arrangement.

items.example_en: In my opinion, that's a bad idea.
items.note: Neutral and everywhere. More formal: на мой взгляд.

items.example_en: It seems to me the situation has changed.
items.note: Russian punctuation puts a comma before что, always.

items.english: I consider that, I hold that
items.example: Я считаю, что дебатам не хватает нюансов.
items.example_en: I think the debate lacks nuance.
items.note: Stronger than думаю: a considered position.

items.example_en: I'm sure this will work.
items.note: Short adjective: уверен, уверена, уверены.

items.example: Тем не менее, стоимость остаётся проблемой.
items.example_en: Nevertheless, the cost is still a problem.
items.note: Signals the concession that follows.

items.example: Это дорого; с другой стороны, служит долго.
items.example_en: It's expensive; on the other hand, it lasts a long time.
items.note: Pairs with с одной стороны, on the one hand.

items.example: Я с тобой согласен в этом вопросе.
items.example_en: I agree with you on this question.
items.note: Short adjective agreeing with the speaker: согласен, согласна.

items.example: Честно говоря, меня это не убеждает.
items.example_en: Honestly, that doesn't convince me.
items.note: Polite disagreement without confrontation.

items.example: Конечно, это рискованно, но бездействие тоже.
items.example_en: Of course it's risky, but so is doing nothing.
items.note: In конечно the ч sounds like sh.

items.example_en: We need to be realistic about the deadlines.
items.note: быть in the infinitive takes an instrumental complement: реалистами.

items.target: если бы у меня был выбор
items.example: Если бы у меня был выбор, я бы сделал иначе.
items.example_en: If I had a choice, I'd do it differently.
items.note: The Russian conditional is one form: past tense plus бы in both halves.

items.example: Как бы то ни было, решать надо сегодня.
items.example_en: Be that as it may, we have to decide today.
items.note: A fixed high-register expression, common in written argument.
